    sample = b"".join(bytes(h)[:int(tok.build_bytes)] for h in heads)

REPLACE WITH:

    heads = area_heads.values() if hasattr(area_heads, "values") else area_heads
    _build_bytes = int(tok.build_bytes)
    if _build_bytes < 1:
        # A SLICE BOUND IS NOT A COUNT UNLESS IT IS POSITIVE. `h[:n]` at n < 0 is Python for "all
        # but the last |n| bytes", so this lever's declared meaning -- "How many bytes are taken
        # from the head of each corpus" -- silently inverts: measured at -1, the build ran to
        # completion on a different sample and returned size 430 / bytes_per_token
        # 3.962156372724027 against 432 / 4.0, with nothing saying the head was not the head. At 0
        # and at large negatives the sample is empty and the run dies two frames down in
        # spine/derive.py::bytes_per_token with "n_tokens=0 -- cannot measure compression over zero
        # tokens", naming no lever, no environment variable and no package. bytes_per_token is the
        # one estimator that leaves this package (spine/derive.py::signature_width_bytes).
        raise LeverError(
            f"TOK_BUILD_BYTES={_build_bytes} is below 1. It is a slice bound on the head of each "
            f"corpus and a negative one takes all but the LAST |n| bytes instead: measured at -1, "
            f"the build returned size 430 and bytes_per_token 3.962156372724027 against 432 and "
            f"4.0 at the default, silently, on a sample that was not the head. At 0 the sample is "
            f"empty and the run dies in spine/derive.py::bytes_per_token naming no lever. Set a "
            f"positive byte count; this bounds nothing from above.")
    sample = b"".join(bytes(h)[:_build_bytes] for h in heads)
